subject: Urgent: P99/P95 spike — Hosted API latency increase, likely KV lookup sparsity
msg_1_subject: Observed p99 jumps on hosted API - impacting checkout flows
msg_1_body:
Hi Rachel,

We started seeing a sustained p95/p99 increase on the Hosted API around 15:40 PT today which is impacting our checkout latency. p95 moved from ~220ms to ~1.1s and p99 breached 1.8s. Error rate climbed from 0.03% to ~0.8% during the spike. This is hitting our product search -> add-to-cart path and causing user drop-off.

Attached is a screenshot of our graphs and a few short traces from our client side that show long tail server times (user-traces-20270721.png). Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? We are in a high-traffic window and need quick mitigation.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Engineering, BrightRetail
msg_2_subject: Re: Observed p99 jumps on hosted API - impacting checkout flows
msg_2_body:
Emma — sorry to hear this. I'm escalating immediately and looping in SRE/Platform. First pass: could you confirm the affected endpoints and a sample request ID if available?

Quick plan: 1) SRE will pull KV/prefix-cache metrics (miss rate, eviction rate, TTLs) and look for a correlated spike. 2) If we see mass invalidations we can temporarily route traffic to a warmed variant and bump cache TTLs while we repair. 3) We'll provide an ETA for mitigation within 30 minutes.

We're treating this as urgent — I have Marissa on the thread for exec visibility.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
msg_3_subject: Re: Observed p99 jumps — initial SRE findings
msg_3_body:
On Wed, Jul 21, 2027 at 4:20 PM Rachel Kim wrote:
> Emma — sorry to hear this. I'm escalating immediately ...

Quick diagnostic summary: I pulled host and runtime metrics for the time window Emma provided. We see a sharp rise in KV lookup latency and miss rate starting 15:36 PT across the us-hosted pool. Miss rate on the prefix cache jumped by ~22x and eviction pressure spiked concurrently. There was a scheduled metadata GC that ran at 15:35 which appears to have cleared several hot prefix entries prematurely.

Evidence attached: kv-invalidation-log-20270721.txt and a snapshot of the p95 dashboard (p95-dashboard-20270721.png).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low risk):
- Stop the problematic GC job and roll back the recent metadata config change (config id: meta-gc-20270721).
- Increase prefix cache TTL from 5m -> 30m for the affected pool to allow warm-up to recover.
- Seed the cache for BrightRetail's top 100 prefixes (script included in mitigation-commands.txt).

If we can apply these steps we expect p95 to fall back within 10–20 minutes, p99 within 30–60 minutes as the KV cache warms. If roll back is not feasible quickly we can route BrightRetail traffic to a warmed dedicated lane (requires a short config flip).

I'll start executing the safe steps now and will post logs as I go.

— Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
msg_4_subject: Re: Observed p99 jumps on hosted API - immediate mitigation in progress
msg_4_body:
Emma — quick update: Marcus identified a metadata GC that triggered mass prefix invalidations. We're applying the low-risk mitigations now (stop GC, bump TTL, seed top prefixes). Marcus expects p95 improvement within 10–20 minutes.

If you have a preferred request ID or example trace that showed the worst latency, please send it and we'll prioritize those prefixes. We'll keep this thread updated and will follow up with a postmortem once we have full root cause analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is bad timing.

— Rachel
msg_5_subject: Post-incident note: BrightRetail p99 spike — next steps and owners
msg_5_body:
Team — thank you for the quick response. Brief summary for leadership:
- Impact: BrightRetail observed p95->1.1s and p99->1.8s for ~20–60 minutes during a metadata GC-induced prefix cache invalidation.
- Mitigation taken: GC stopped, prefix TTL increased, cache seeding executed; customer traffic routed to warmed lane briefly.
- Current state: metrics returned to baseline on 07/21 by 17:10 PT; BrightRetail confirmed recovery.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: produce a short RCA and include timeline + change (due 07/24).
- Dylan: add guardrails to metadata GC to prevent mass invalidation windows (due 07/31).
- Neha: coordinate follow-up with BrightRetail (credit/SLAs conversation if requested) and confirm they received a full summary (due 07/23).

Please add any missing items. I'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem sync if needed.

— Marissa
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
